gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 1 mini-boss role, former dock worker backstory, gear and the five named moves are canon (lore item brick-dugan). Stats, telegraph timings, tier, look palette and the low-health trigger threshold are invented because the GDD gives no numbers. Tier 2 (the player's first major skill check, so above Breaker HP but below the Overseers).
name: "Brick" Dugan
description: A broad former dock worker recruited into the Rust, built like a human battering ram. Heavy black security vest with the Rust insignia, riot-control shoulder pads, reinforced forearm guards, steel-toe boots and a utility belt of restraints and radio gear. Boxy and symmetrical, slate and gunmetal tones, narrow cyan visor. Lore: brick-dugan.
behaviour: Slow but intimidating and easy to read. Walks Zed down, uses Brick Breaker Punch up close, Running Shoulder Charge along a lane from range, Ground Stomp when Zed is airborne or crowding him, and Grab and Wall Slam if Zed stays in melee range too long. Below 30 percent health (proposed threshold) he enters Rage Punch mode: one extra-heavy punch, still telegraphed. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity so juggles cannot loop him.
telegraph: Brick Breaker Punch 650 ms: fist drawn back, shoulders squared. Running Shoulder Charge 800 ms: he lowers his shoulder and scrapes a boot, red ground strip along the lane. Ground Stomp 700 ms: knee lifts high, red circle under his boots. Grab and Wall Slam 600 ms: both arms open wide, red icon. Rage Punch 900 ms: longer wind-up with a held fist and a bigger red icon.
weakness: Dodge sideways out of the charge lane and he crashes into the arena wall, leaving a long recovery to punish. Jump the Ground Stomp, back-step the grab. Do not trade blows head-on: block the punch, then hit him in recovery. Teaches dodging as the first real skill check.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 2 (Transit District) mini-boss role, former transit security officer, electrified baton, armoured trench coat, scanner visor, five named moves and the stun-mechanics role are canon (lore item railgun-royce). Stats, timings, tier, stun duration and Rail Trap layout are invented.
name: "Railgun" Royce
description: A former transit security officer in a long armoured trench coat, slate with gunmetal panels, carrying an electrified baton and wearing a scanner visor that glows cyan. Upright, symmetrical, boxy shoulders. Lore: railgun-royce.
behaviour: Mid-range controller who introduces stun. Opens with a Baton Combo, closes distance with a Charging Dash, answers a crowding Zed with Shockwave Slam, and lays Rail Trap electrified floor strips that block part of the lane for a few seconds (proposed 4 s). Taser Burst is a short-range stun shot. Being stunned briefly locks Zed's inputs (proposed 600 ms), never more, so the player learns to avoid rather than die to it. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
telegraph: Baton Combo 500 ms: baton raised and crackling. Charging Dash 650 ms: crouch with the visor flashing, red ground strip. Shockwave Slam 750 ms: baton planted overhead, red circle around him. Rail Trap 800 ms: he kneels and a cyan line marks the floor strip before it electrifies. Taser Burst 550 ms: arm extends, visor locks on with a red icon.
weakness: Stay off the marked Rail Trap strips and dodge the Taser Burst by moving out of line. Parry or jump the dash, then heavy-attack him in the long recovery after Shockwave Slam. Rewards reading the floor and the dodge.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 3 (Industrial Zone) mini-boss role, chief enforcer to Rhea Calder, hydraulic work suit, industrial hammer, five named moves and the role of preparing players for Calder are canon (lore item crusher-kane). Stats, timings, tier and steam vent geometry are invented. Deliberately a slower, heavier version of the grunt's timing, foreshadowing Calder's 900 ms telegraphs.
name: "Crusher" Kane
description: Rhea Calder's chief enforcer in a bulky hydraulic work suit, slate with gunmetal pistons and steam pipes along the arms, swinging a huge industrial hammer. Visor slit glows cyan. Symmetrical, boxy and slow-moving. Lore: crusher-kane; serves rust-overseer-calder.
behaviour: Heavy slow bruiser who previews Calder. Hammer Slam is his main attack, Hook Chain Grab pulls Zed in from range, Furnace Kick is a short sweeping kick, Steam Vent Burst vents a cone of steam from the suit that leaves a hazard patch (proposed 3 s), Crushing Uppercut launches Zed upward if he is standing close. Slow movement, long recoveries. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
telegraph: Hammer Slam 850 ms: hammer lifted overhead with a red ground circle. Hook Chain Grab 700 ms: chain whirls above his head and the hook flashes, red icon. Furnace Kick 600 ms: leg pulls back, steam hisses from the knee. Steam Vent Burst 900 ms: suit shakes and steam builds on the shoulders, red cone on the ground. Crushing Uppercut 750 ms: hammer swung low behind him, red strip in front.
weakness: Dodge out of the red circle and strike during the long Hammer Slam recovery. Break line of sight on the Hook Chain, stay out of steam patches. Back away from the uppercut and punish. Trains the player to wait for big telegraphs before Overseer Calder.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 4 (Neon Market) mini-boss role, former hacker turned Rust cyber operative, holographic mask, portable drone pack, five named moves and the role of introducing Voss's deception mechanics are canon (lore item glitch). Stats, timings, tier, clone count and teleport rules are invented. Drones he launches reuse rust-voss-drone and his Hologram Duplicate reuses rust-hologram-decoy.
name: "Glitch"
description: A former hacker turned Rust cyber operative, thinner than other Rust units, slate uniform under a flickering holographic mask and a portable drone pack on his back with cyan indicator lights. Still symmetrical and boxy at the shoulders. Lore: glitch; previews rust-overseer-voss.
behaviour: Evasive deception fighter who keeps his distance. Drone Barrage launches a small volley of drones (reuses the Voss drone unit, proposed 2 at a time), Hologram Duplicate creates one decoy of himself that throws a weak punch (reuses the hologram decoy), Shock Disk Throw is a straight ranged projectile, Data Spike is a short ground line attack. Emergency Teleport triggers when Zed gets close or health drops past a threshold (proposed 50 percent): he blinks to the far side of the arena with a brief vulnerable pause on arrival. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
telegraph: Drone Barrage 700 ms: pack opens and lights blink, red icon above the pack. Hologram Duplicate 500 ms: mask flickers and the decoy shimmers into place. Shock Disk Throw 550 ms: disk spun up in his hand, red line of flight. Data Spike 600 ms: he crouches and a cyan line draws on the floor before the spike. Emergency Teleport 400 ms: mask static then a cyan flash, and a 700 ms vulnerable pause on arrival.
weakness: Pick out the real Glitch (the decoy's outline wobbles and it has no pack), dodge the disk line and punish him right after the teleport arrival. Breaking the drones with a quick combo keeps pressure off. Introduces the 'which one is real' skill before Overseer Voss.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 5 (Skyline District) mini-boss role, Silas Wren's personal hunter, grapple launcher, lightweight armour, five named moves and the role of training vertical combat are canon (lore item raptor). Stats, timings, tier and the look (slate, light plating) are invented. Fast and fragile compared with Kane, mirroring Wren's 400 ms telegraphs.
name: "Raptor"
description: Silas Wren's personal hunter in lightweight slate armour with a shoulder-mounted grapple launcher, a swept-back visor and a narrow, agile frame. Cold hue, symmetrical, boxy plates kept light. Lore: raptor; serves rust-overseer-wren.
behaviour: Fast vertical attacker. Dive Kick drops from a jump onto Zed's position, Wall Bounce Strike rebounds off the arena edge into a diagonal strike, Grapple Pull yanks Zed a short way, Aerial Barrage is a flurry of kicks in the air, Falcon Drop is a high leap followed by a heavy slam on a marked spot. Often airborne, so ground-only attacks miss him. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
telegraph: Dive Kick 450 ms: crouch and jump with a red ground marker where he will land. Wall Bounce Strike 500 ms: he skids toward the wall and flashes the visor. Grapple Pull 550 ms: launcher raised, a thin cyan cable line to Zed. Aerial Barrage 600 ms: he rises with legs pulled up, red icon overhead. Falcon Drop 800 ms: he leaps off-screen with a long shadow growing on the ground before the slam.
weakness: Anti-air hits and jump attacks catch him in the air, and the red ground marker shows exactly where to step away from. Dodge the cable line, then punish his landing recovery. Trains vertical awareness before Overseer Wren.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 6 (Undercity) mini-boss role, failed chemical test subject of Dr. Holt, mutated physique, back chemical tanks, glowing green veins, five named moves and the area-denial role are canon (lore item holts-experiment-subject-88). Stats, timings, tier and hazard sizes are invented. Subject 88 is a person from Holt's experiments, not a monster: describe him with care, no gore. Green glow is canon; Overload Violet is reserved for phase-2 power glows and is not used here.
name: Dr. Holt's Experiment "Subject 88"
description: A hulking, hunched test subject from Dr. Holt's experiments, with a mutated physique, chemical tanks strapped to the back and glowing green veins along the arms and neck. Torn Rust-issue clothing hangs off the shoulders. Confused and in distress rather than cruel. Lore: holts-experiment-subject-88; ties to rust-overseer-holt.
behaviour: Area-denial bruiser. Toxic Breath is a short cone of gas that lingers, Acid Spit lobs a puddle at Zed's position (proposed 3 s), Frenzied Charge is a lane charge when he flares, Corrosion Slam is a heavy overhead strike that leaves a small puddle, Chemical Explosion bursts from the tanks in a ring at low health (proposed 40 percent) and is the only time he stops advancing. Hazards stay on the ground and slowly fade. Takes an attacker slot before every move.
telegraph: Toxic Breath 600 ms: chest swells and green mist leaks from the tanks. Acid Spit 650 ms: head tilts back, a green circle forms on the ground. Frenzied Charge 800 ms: he roars and the veins brighten, red lane strip. Corrosion Slam 750 ms: both fists raised, red circle. Chemical Explosion 1000 ms: tanks glow brighter and rattle, ring warning grows on the floor.
weakness: Keep moving: hazards punish standing still. Dodge the lane charge into the wall, then heavy-attack in recovery. Step out of the ring before the Chemical Explosion and hit him afterward. Rewards positioning and spacing.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 7 (Rust Military Compound) mini-boss role, leader of the Copper Fangs, elite black armour, tactical shield, twin electrified gauntlets, five named moves (including Fang Protocol calling in Specialists) and the 'toughest non-boss enemy' claim are canon (lore item commander-atlas). Stats, timings, tier, Specialist count and phase thresholds are invented. Deliberately tuned above rust-copper-fang (140 HP) and below Overseers to honour 'toughest non-boss'.
name: Commander Atlas
description: The leader of the Copper Fangs: elite black armour with copper-toned gauntlets, a large tactical shield and twin electrified gauntlets, a hard symmetrical helmet with a narrow cyan visor. The sharpest, most composed Rust unit in the game. Lore: commander-atlas; leads rust-copper-fang units.
behaviour: Disciplined shield-and-gauntlet duelist. Shield Bash opens and breaks Zed's guard, Gauntlet Combo is a fast 3-hit string, Grapple Hook Pull yanks Zed in, Electric Counter is a stance that punishes mashed attacks while he holds the shield up, and Fang Protocol calls in Specialists (proposed 2 rust-copper-fang units, never more than 2 on screen, called once per phase). Below 50 percent health he drops the shield stance for faster gauntlet strings. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
telegraph: Shield Bash 550 ms: shield pulled in, red ground strip in front. Gauntlet Combo 400 ms: gauntlets spark and cross in front of him, each hit has a short flash. Grapple Hook Pull 650 ms: launcher raised, cyan cable line shows the path. Electric Counter 500 ms: shield held up with crackling gauntlets, red shield-edge flash if Zed attacks into it. Fang Protocol 900 ms: he raises one fist and a signal flare pulses, Specialists arrive after 1200 ms.
weakness: Wait out the Electric Counter stance rather than mashing, dodge the cable line, then heavy-attack to break the shield. Parry the Gauntlet Combo's first hit to open a juggle. Defeating or avoiding the Specialists first reduces pressure. Rewards patience and parrying, the full toolkit of block, dodge, parry and combos.

gddGap: CANON/PROPOSED SPLIT: name, Level 8 (Corporate Tower) mini-boss role, experimental combat android protecting Varr, Rust insignia, chest energy core, five named moves, the phase-2 core overload (faster attacks, red laser barrage, explosive dash attacks) and its role as the final challenge before Varr are canon (lore item sentinel-x9). Stats, timings, tier, Self-Repair rate and phase threshold are invented. The GDD's red laser barrage conflicts with the owner decision that phase-2 power glows use Overload Violet and enemy bodies never use red: the barrage is drawn Overload Violet with a Telegraph Red ground warning (open question for the owner). It is a machine, so it is powered down rather than destroyed on defeat.
name: Sentinel-X9
description: An experimental corporate combat android, tall and perfectly symmetrical, with slate and steel plating, a Rust insignia on the chest plate and a round energy core glowing cyan in the chest. Visor slit cyan. In phase 2 the core overloads and glows Overload Violet with cracks of light along the plating. Lore: sentinel-x9; protects rust-halden-varr.
behaviour: Mechanical, rhythmic and precise. Laser Sweep arcs a beam across the lane from the eyes, Rocket Punch fires a fist forward in a straight line and it returns, Ground Pound is a heavy slam with a shockwave ring, Energy Shield blocks front hits until a heavy break, Self-Repair Mode rises when health is low and heals slowly while he is stationary (proposed 5 HP per second for up to 4 s, interruptible). Phase 2 (below 50 percent health): faster attacks, a Laser Sweep that becomes a laser barrage (multiple beams) and explosive dash attacks. Takes an attacker slot before every move. Boss hitstun immunity.
telegraph: Laser Sweep 700 ms: head turns, eyes charge cyan, red arc on the ground. Rocket Punch 600 ms: arm retracts with a whine, red lane strip. Ground Pound 800 ms: both fists rise overhead, red ring around him. Energy Shield 400 ms: core flares and a shield bubble forms. Self-Repair Mode 500 ms: panels open and green sparks. Phase 2 laser barrage 600 ms and explosive dash 450 ms (faster), each with a violet core pulse and red ground warning.
weakness: Heavy attacks break the Energy Shield, interrupt Self-Repair with a burst of damage before it heals, and dodge the lane strips. Phase 2 punishes standing still but its shorter pauses after the dash give a clear opening. A final test of block, dodge, parry and combos before Halden Varr.
